steps.title: Main regions
steps.body: Spain has the most, mainly in Jumilla, Yecla, Alicante and Valencia, as Monastrell. In France, it's the star of Bandol in Provence and a partner in the southern Rhône and Languedoc. Australia grows it in the Barossa and McLaren Vale; California in Contra Costa and Paso Robles.

steps.title: Blending
steps.body: Mourvèdre is the M in GSM blends, with Grenache and Syrah. Grenache brings red fruit and alcohol, Syrah colour and spice, Mourvèdre tannin, dark fruit and a savoury frame that helps the blend age. In Châteauneuf-du-Pape, some estates use a high share, like Château de Beaucastel.

steps.prompt: What does Mourvèdre bring to a GSM blend?
steps.explanation: Mourvèdre adds structure and savoury depth; Grenache brings red fruit.

steps.title: Climate
steps.body: Mourvèdre needs a long, hot season, often harvested in October. It likes sea breezes and some water near the roots, which is why coastal Bandol suits it. It's drought-tolerant once established, and resists oxidation in winemaking. On its own roots in sandy soils, it survives in parts of Spain.

steps.explanation: In cool, short seasons it won't ripen.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Spain grows the most, as Monastrell
Mourvèdre is the M in GSM, adding structure
It needs heat, a long season and likes the sea
